legal.title: Accessibility is <hl>a right</hl>
legal.subtitle: Under Brazil's Decree 12.773/25, inclusive education is a guaranteed right — and AdaptaEDU helps schools deliver on that commitment in practice.
legal.p1: Support services and resources for students with disabilities are rights guaranteed by Brazilian law at every stage, level and modality of basic education. They do not replace teaching in the regular classroom; on the contrary, they complement and strengthen the educational process, helping to remove barriers — attitudinal, architectural, communication, informational, technological and pedagogical — and to promote full participation in school life.
legal.quote1: Educating is opening doors; including is making sure no one is left outside.
legal.quote2: Inclusion is our ability to understand and recognize others and, in doing so, to have the privilege of living alongside and sharing with people who are different from us.
legal.p2: The services that must be offered include Specialized Educational Services (AEE, Atendimento Educacional Especializado), school support professionals and multifunctional resource rooms (SRMs). Diverse teaching strategies, accessible teaching materials and assistive technologies are also essential. That is exactly where AdaptaEDU fits: as an assistive technology that turns teaching materials into accessible resources, automatically and at scale.

items.a: AdaptaEDU is an artificial intelligence platform that automatically adapts educational materials for 9 accessibility profiles: autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, central auditory processing disorder (CAPD), intellectual disability, low vision, dyslexia, dyscalculia, dysgraphia and giftedness. Teachers upload PDFs or DOCX files and receive adapted versions in minutes.

AdaptaEDU is built for regular classroom teachers, AEE (Specialized Educational Services) teachers, pedagogical coordinators and leaders of private and public schools, as well as school networks. Individual teachers adapt on their own with the Teacher plan; schools centralize teachers, content and metrics with the School plan.

items.q: How does adaptation via WhatsApp work?
items.a: The teacher takes a photo of the textbook page, worksheet or test, sends it to AdaptaEDU's WhatsApp number and states the student's profile, for example "adapt for dyslexia". Within minutes, the adapted material comes back as a PDF in the same chat.

items.q: How do you adapt school materials for autistic students?
items.a: For students with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), AdaptaEDU automatically applies a predictable visual structure, fewer distracting stimuli, clear and literal instructions and consistent visual supports. Just upload the material and select the ASD profile.

items.q: What is AEE and how does AdaptaEDU help?
items.a: AEE (Atendimento Educacional Especializado, or Specialized Educational Services) is the Brazilian education service that ensures students with disabilities, autism and giftedness can access what the rest of the class learns, usually in multifunctional resource rooms (SRMs) and outside regular class hours. AdaptaEDU automates the most time-consuming part of AEE: turning each material into accessible versions for the student's profile while preserving the learning objective.

items.q: Does AdaptaEDU comply with inclusive education law?
items.a: Yes. AdaptaEDU was built in compliance with Brazil's Decree 12.773/25 and Brazilian inclusive education law, which guarantees students with disabilities the right to accessible teaching materials and assistive technologies at every stage of basic education.

items.q: How much does AdaptaEDU cost for schools?
items.a: The Teacher plan costs R$150/month (Brazilian reais) with 30 adaptations per month and 3 trial adaptations included. The School plan costs R$1,250/month, with 250 adaptations per month, 5 trial adaptations included, multi-tenant teacher management, all 9 accessibility profiles and a metrics dashboard. School networks get custom pricing.

items.q: What file types does AdaptaEDU accept?
items.a: AdaptaEDU accepts PDFs, DOCX documents and images. Adapted material can be exported as PDF or DOCX, ready to hand out to students.

items.q: How does AdaptaEDU help private schools?
items.a: For private schools, AdaptaEDU offers an admin account with centralized teacher management, usage control, content packages by grade level (elementary, middle and high school) and a metrics dashboard — a competitive edge that meets families' expectations for real inclusion.

aee.title: Adapting isn't making it easier. <hl>It's opening the way.</hl>
aee.subtitle: AEE (Specialized Educational Services, Brazil's support service for students with disabilities) exists so that every student can access what the whole class learns. But in a busy week, the question remains: where do you start? Here are the four steps that make an adaptation work.

aluno.title: Start with the student, not the activity
aluno.text: Before touching any worksheet, look at who will receive it. The right adaptation comes from the answers to three questions:
items: What can they already do independently?

barreira.title: Name the barrier
barreira.text: When an activity doesn't work, the problem is almost never the student — it's something between them and the content. And each barrier calls for a different response.

adapte.title: Adapt without losing the meaning
adapte.text: Fewer questions, more direct instructions, a different format: anything goes, as long as the learning objective stays. Adapting changes the path, never the destination.
items: Reduce the quantity or complexity — never the essential objective.
Use visual supports and concrete materials.
Rely on assistive technology: adapted keyboards, special mice, reading software.

junto.title: Do it together
junto.text: Inclusion isn't a one-person job. Every teacher has a role — and partnership is what moves the student forward.

cognitiva.name: Cognitive

sensorial.name: Sensory
sensorial.sign: Materials or stimuli are uncomfortable or get in the way.

motora.name: Motor
motora.sign: Writing, holding or handling things is difficult.

comunicacao.name: Communication
comunicacao.sign: They know the answer but can't express it.

comum.does: Leads the lesson and adapts content for the class.

aee.does: Works behind the scenes and outside class hours: advises, produces accessible materials and suggests strategies.

cta.title: Step 3 takes the most time. Leave that one to us.
cta.text: Send the material, choose the student's profile and get the adapted version — with the learning objective preserved — in minutes. That leaves time for what no AI can replace: getting to know the student and planning together.

quemSomos.title: We were born in a <hl>classroom</hl>
quemSomos.subtitle: AdaptaEDU exists because adapting material for each student is too much work to fit into a teacher's routine — and too important to be left out of it.
quemSomos.mission: Put accessible teaching materials in every teacher's hands, in minutes — so that adaptation no longer depends on time nobody has and becomes a natural part of lesson preparation.
quemSomos.vision: A school where no student is left out of a lesson for lack of material suited to the way they learn — and where accessibility is routine, not the exception.

andrea.credencial: Educator (University of São Paulo), inclusion specialist (UNICAMP)
bio: Her work in inclusion began in 1993, at one of Brazil's pioneering inclusive schools. She holds a degree in education from the University of São Paulo (USP) and is an inclusion specialist trained at UNICAMP and at the Reference Center for Learning Disorders.

She co-authored "Caminhos pedagógicos da inclusão" (Pedagogical Paths to Inclusion), on how quality education for all is being implemented in Brazilian schools (Editora Memnon). Today she teaches in the early grades and in AEE, Brazil's specialized educational services.
She provides the pedagogical foundation that makes adaptation work for each student profile.
He specialized in artificial intelligence in Canada in 2017. Two years later he founded Bettrads, a generative AI hub whose results outperformed GPT-3 benchmarks.

Today he is CPO and co-founder of MyDataAgent, Brazil's first platform for autonomous AI agents. He leads the engineering that makes adapting a material take minutes — and keeps it that way when there are thousands of them.
